claims: Independently read the ICON-01-HOURGLASS contract, confirmed its completed dependency, and inspected the complete five-file diff on the exact clean candidate.
Canonical agent-scope verification passed against base c3619da6b431398e70662458ba5605761e18fb20; git diff --check also passed. No product or task-status edits were made by the verifier.
All three shipped source images are 1024 by 1024 RGB PNGs without alpha; the Watch artwork is byte-identical to iPhone light and iPhone dark has a distinct digest.
The iPhone primary AppIcon catalog contains an Any/default image and a dark image selected by the native luminosity dark appearance; the Watch catalog retains one matching watchOS image.
Full-resolution inspection confirms coherent hourglass geometry, navy/slate caps, teal glass, amber sand and a centered stream, with a warm light background and charcoal dark background.
Independent source previews at 160, 60, 40 and 29 pixels retain a recognizable hourglass in both appearances; a circular Watch mask preserves the complete subject with safe space around its caps.
The shipped dark PNG has no checkerboard pattern or transparent corners; the rejected intermediate is not referenced or added by this change.

WAT-30 documents generation prompts, sips normalization, the rejected checkerboard intermediate, native appearance selection, and separate compilation, signed-package and physical-validation boundaries.
The diff changes only the two app-icon sets and provenance documentation; app behavior, signing, bundle identifiers, privacy declarations and version/build values remain unchanged.
limitations: This receipt is bounded source and visual verification. It does not prove asset-catalog compilation, installed Home Screen appearance selection, Watch launcher rendering, signed packaging or physical-device behavior.
The scaled preview uses diagnostic resizing and illustrative masks; it is not a native device screenshot or compiled asset rendition.
Fine glass highlights and sand texture simplify at the smallest sizes while the hourglass silhouette remains recognizable.
The candidate retains version 0.2.0 build 5; subsequent version allocation and builds require their own exact-source evidence.

authorityReference.reference: 2026-09-06 owner request to replace the existing app icon with the hourglass artwork and native iPhone light/dark appearances, as recorded in ICON-01-HOURGLASS and WAT-30-HOURGLASS-ICON.md.
